props.title: The Long Riders
props.initialSlug: Outlaw James brothers ride and rob in the Old West

sections.content: The Long Riders revolutionized the Western genre by casting actual brothers to play historical outlaw siblings. Director Walter Hill's masterstroke of featuring the Keach, Carradine, Guest, and Quaid brothers brought unprecedented authenticity to this brutal retelling of the James-Younger gang. The film's violence, particularly the Northfield raid sequence, drew heavily from Sam Peckinpah's techniques in The Wild Bunch (1969), with Hill employing slow-motion photography to heighten the impact of bullets and blood. This approach influenced later Westerns like Unforgiven (1992) and The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford (2007).

sections.content: The film's portrayal of post-Civil War tensions marked a significant shift from earlier James gang films like Jesse James (1939). Where previous versions romanticized the outlaws as Robin Hood figures, Hill's interpretation showed them as complex Confederate veterans struggling with a changing America. This darker approach influenced later revisionist Westerns like Open Range (2003) and The Hateful Eight (2015), which similarly explored violence as both personal and political expression.

Hill's attention to period detail and authentic Missouri/Kansas border culture set new standards for historical Westerns. The film's use of folk music and traditional instruments, performed by Ry Cooder, created a template followed by Tombstone (1993) and True Grit (2010) in using period-appropriate music to enhance authenticity rather than simply scoring dramatic moments. sections.content: The film's exploration of family loyalty amid violence created a new template for Western storytelling. The real-life brother casting wasn't just a gimmick - it added layers of meaning to scenes of familial bonds tested by criminal life. This influenced later Westerns like 3:10 to Yuma (2007) and The Sisters Brothers (2018) in their examination of brotherhood and loyalty in lawless territories.
